 Follow Todd Chrisley Fights To Keep Son’s Drug Test Records Out Of Crash Lawsuit
 Chukwudi Onyewuchi Fri, October 23, 2026 at 2:40 PM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/MEGA Todd Chrisley 's account of his son's hospital visit has become part of a legal fight over what the other driver can examine.
 Grayson Chrisley , who was involved in a 2022 Tennessee crash, says he underwent drug and alcohol testing afterward.
 Now the family is resisting efforts by the man suing them to obtain those records, arguing they have little bearing on the damages dispute. The disagreement puts a private medical file at the center of the lawsuit.
 Todd Chrisley's Crash Account Became A Point Of Dispute Over Records
 Abbas Shirmohammadi – Panoramic Visions for CNP / MEGA
 Patrick Rykwalder, who sued Grayson, Todd, Julie and Savannah Chrisley over the collision, wants access to Grayson's medical and testing records.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In court filings obtained by TMZ , Rykwalder argued the documents could help him investigate the crash and assess claims about Grayson's condition.
 Rykwalder's request also drew on Todd Chrisley's public account of the aftermath. Todd reportedly discussed the wreck on his podcast in November 2022, saying he went to the scene and accompanied his son to the hospital, where he arranged for a toxicology test.
 Rykwalder also pointed to Grayson's reported concussion, arguing the medical file could help establish whether that injury occurred.
 The Chrisleys, however, opposed disclosure, maintaining that the records were not relevant to determining damages and that Grayson had already admitted liability for the accident.
 Todd's Son Was Hospitalized After The Tennessee Crash
 Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/MEGA
 The dispute over Todd Chrisley's son's post-crash medical records turned on what could be established about the collision itself.
 Advertisement Advertisement According to Entertainment Tonight , Grayson was driving on Interstate 65 in Nashville on November 12, 2022, when his Ford F-150 struck a vehicle stopped in traffic.
 The driver of the vehicle hit from behind sustained injuries in the impact but declined ambulance transport to a hospital. Officers asked Grayson what had happened, but he could not recall the crash.
 According to the outlet, the authorities attributed his memory loss to suspected head injuries. Following Grayson's transportation to the hospital, both vehicles were towed.
 Todd Chrisley's Private Messages Became A Separate Discovery Fight
 MEGA
 The crash lawsuit also prompted a dispute over how much of Todd's family's communications could be examined.
 Advertisement Advertisement Rykwalder sought phone records from Todd, Julie, Grayson and Savannah, arguing the communications could help clarify what happened around the collision.
 According to reports, he subpoenaed Verizon and AT&T for call and text records. Todd and Julie opposed the requests, describing them as "unreasonable, oppressive, and a clear effort to harass" them.
 Rykwalder argued the requests were legitimate, pointing to the family's communications around the crash and Todd and Julie's public discussion of it.
 Both parties reportedly reached a narrower arrangement: Grayson's phone records would be produced, while Todd and Julie's records would undergo attorney review, with relevant material disclosed under the agreement.

 The couple also launched a $25 million lawsuit against their former lawyer .

 He previously returned to Instagram to celebrate Grayson's academic milestone .
 Todd and Julie later opened up about how their marriage changed after prison .
 Todd's Lawsuit Against Georgia Official Involved Daughter Lindsie
 Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/MEGA
 The fight over privacy in the crash case echoed another legal dispute in which Todd Chrisley's family relationships were part of the allegations.
 Advertisement Advertisement In 2019, Todd and Julie sued Georgia tax investigator Joshua Waites, accusing him of abusing his position and improperly pursuing their estranged daughter, Lindsie.
 Entertainment Tonight reported that the couple alleged Waites had tried to induce Lindsie to provide compromising information about her family and had shared confidential tax and grand-jury information with her.
 According to the lawsuit, he pursued "an increasingly aggressive relationship with Lindsie." The couple also alleged that the investigator's actions contributed to what they described as "bogus tax evasion claims" against them.
 Todd Chrisley And Julie Reached A $1 Million Georgia Settlement
 MEGA
 The lawsuit Todd and Julie brought against former Georgia tax investigator Joshua Waites ended in a reported $1 million settlement with the State of Georgia.
 Advertisement Advertisement The settlement agreement called for the Georgia Department of Administrative Services to issue two checks totaling $1 million to the Chrisleys' lawyers within 30 days.
 Their attorney, Alex Little, described the payment as "an encouraging sign," adding that the couple had argued their criminal case was unusual and had serious problems.
 However, the settlement did not necessarily mean the Chrisleys would keep the money. In February 2024, reports revealed that the federal government filed a claim for nearly $1 million in settlement proceeds toward the couple's criminal restitution judgment, which exceeded $17 million.
